chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no one who takes a dog except that one qirat (unit of measurement) would be reduced from his deeds every day.

key_terms.قِيرَاطٌ: qirat (a unit of weight or measure, often used metaphorically for deeds)
key_terms.يَتَّخِذُ: to take/keep/adopt (as a pet or for work)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual penalty for keeping a dog according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Reported by the prominent companion Zurarah from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith quantifies the spiritual cost of dog ownership as the daily loss of one 'qirat' of good deeds, reflecting the juristic view that keeping a dog is generally disliked unless for specific utility like hunting or guarding. This daily deduction underscores the continuous nature of spiritual accountability in Shia tradition, linking material possession to immediate metaphysical consequence.
